utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Good afternoon -- good morning, actually, to everybody. Mr. Registrar, please can you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is case number IT-98-34-A, the Prosecutor versus Mladen Naletilic and Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I call for the appearances. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Christopher Staker. I appear on behalf of the Prosecution with my colleague Ms. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen, our case manager today is Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Zelimir Par, a member of the bar. I am accompanied by Mr. Kerns who shall introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERNS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Kurt Kerns on behalf of Mr. Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, appearing for Mr. Naletilic is Mr. Meek. Co-counsel Mr. Hennessy is not available today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask -- so the appellants are present. May I ask Mr. Martinovic if he understands the proceedings or if there is any problem with the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MARTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There aren't any. I can follow them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I wish to recall the purpose of this Status Conference since it is the first time we have a Status Conference in this appeal. According to the Rules, and in particular Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, a Status Conference is convened regularly every 120 days or, of course, more frequently if necessary, to allow the persons in custody pending the appeal an opportunity to raise issues in relation to their custody, including the conditions of the person in custody. And, of course, the second purpose of the Status Conference is to update the appellant with respect of the status of the case or to discuss any relevant matter concerning the preparation of the case. Now, I would ask the appellants, the counsels, if there is any problem relating to the detention of the person they represent, the two appellants.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as the conditions in the Detention Unit are concerned, our client doesn't have any objection at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as the conditions in the Detention Unit are concerned, Mr. Naletilic also has no objections at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. I wish to remind you that should any problem arise, the Rules governing the detention of persons awaiting trial or before the Appeals Chamber allow for a special procedure, a special complaint procedure that you may take note of should the case arise. Now, let's come to the status this appeal. I don't have to recall the briefing schedule. There are some pending deadlines for presentation of briefs both as concerns the briefs, the appeal briefs, and the responses, and as concerns the 115 motions. There is, however, one thing I believe we should deal with, and it is probably the Naletilic 115 motion that has been -- for additional evidence, that has been submitted on the 15th of August. There are two problems there. One problem concerned the documents and the translation of the documents that were submitted in Serbo-Croat without, apparently, I don't know exactly, I would like to be briefed. Was -- perhaps the Defence may clarify whether the translation was requested by the Defence when submitting -- before submitting the motion or not. Please, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I address that issue while you have it fresh on your mind. We did actually, as you know, file the 115 motion with Serbo-Croatian documents. That is because we had just discovered these documents. We could not have them translated in time. It is my understanding that Mr. Hennessy, the lead counsel, was to -- has requested those be translated as soon as possible, but we felt that we had to file at least what we had to make the deadline, with the understanding that we would have those translated as soon as possible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, am I correct, if I understand it, a translation has been now made and submitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: To clarify, Your Honour, I believe that they are in the translation unit but they have not been completed. The translation has not been completed to date. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I understand part of the translation has been made but not all of them probably. I don't know whether -- has it been submitted or not? It is submitted. Well, I understand the translation has been completed. I don't know whether it has been regularly submitted, whether it has reached the Prosecution or not. May I have the Prosecution view on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has received a filing which does contain English translations of this material. We've not yet verified whether it's complete, but that may well be the case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, with that in mind, I would ask that those translated documents be placed in my locker box 144, because I have not received the translated -- English translations back yet. Perhaps I could get a copy of those after the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. This question will be clarified, but as I understand it, it is simply a question of simply having it put at the disposal of the parties if there is any problem of this kind. So, the second question I wanted to deal with concerns the filing of the 115 motion itself. There has been a response to that motion presented by the Prosecution challenging the format of the motion and asking either to dismiss the motion or to -- or that the motion be refiled regularly. May I have perhaps the Prosecution seeing if this -- if this is correct or if they want to clarify better the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution position was set out in the response filed on the 19th of August, the Prosecution submission being that the motion should be dismissed in its entirety for the reasons given in our response. We did take an alternative submission in the event that that primary submission was not accepted by the Chamber, but the primary submission is that it should be dismissed in its entirety and we submit that this is because parties should not be encouraged to file motions in defective form in the expectation that they will then be given an opportunity after the deadline has passed to put it in order. Where there is a deadline for filing a motion, we submit the responsibility is on the party to file it in proper form within the deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Staker. May I ask Mr. Meek the views of the Defence on this question. If I understand, no reply has been filed to the Prosecutor's response so far. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, you were. We have not filed a response. That does not mean, in any fashion, that we agree with what the Prosecution filed. We believe that the form was not defective. Honestly, Your Honour, we submitted and I told you earlier today that we filed those documents not in English because we didn't have a translation. They have apparently now been translated. We believe that the response of the Prosecutor is a boilerplate response. They deny any relevance which we expected them to deny relevance. They denied relevance to most of our documents but that doesn't make -- just because they make that allegation we don't believe it's true. If you'd like a response to that, we'd be happy to file a response. But our response would be that we think the Prosecution is out of line and there is no merit to their motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek. I don't ask you to file a reply to that. I just wanted to have your views because indeed apparently my position is that -- is that the -- the motion you filed is in compliance with Article 115 but not with the practice direction concerning the filing of 115 motions, with Rule 11 of the practice direction on formal requirements for appeals from judgement, which would ask the party submitting additional evidence to be more precise in indicating a number of requirements. And I think parties should essentially comply with this practice direction because otherwise, the dealing with the appeal and with the evidence becomes more difficult. So on this question, my inclination would be to accept the Prosecutor's position that the motion is not in accordance with the practice direction and to decide exacting the alternative proposal of the Prosecution, that is to set to the Defence of Mr. Naletilic a short deadline to refile the 115 motion in full accord with the practice direction, taking into account the practice direction. And of course, the Prosecution would be entitled to respond to that motion as of the date in which it will be filed, in which the 115 will be refiled. This is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Staker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Just a question by way of clarification. Would that decision apply to the real 115 motion proper? Because there is a separate issue in relation to the supplement to the Rule 115 motion which, as we noticed, was filed after the deadline and also contained material which clearly was available at trial. Our objections weren't addressed simply to the form of the motion, they also went to the substance of compliance with Rule 115 and in case of the supplement, I think that arises in a fairly immediate way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, I will -- I will have to reflect on the supplement, actually. I will reserve on the supplement. But as to the motion -- sorry. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour, I believe the document that Mr. Staker is referring to, while he states to this Court that it was available during trial, I believe it was delivered to the Defence during the rebuttal case. So it wasn't available to us during the trial. It was given to us at the last moment by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Well, I will rule on that after having further consideration. But as to the 115 motion itself, I will -- I think that a few days will be sufficient to refile it, and I'm -- I don't want to delay the proceedings too much for a refiling simply. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, I've -- I'm travelling tomorrow. God willing, I'll be back in the United States. Due to press with other legal business. There is probably no way I could refile that in a few days. We have a final brief due on the 15th. It's a tremendous task, and I would ask for more time, Your Honour. I'll be given the English translations of the actual documents for the Rule 115 today I presume, so I can attach those and put it in the proper form, but I would ask for more than a few days, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I take into account your consideration. However, we are in the presence of a filing that, in my view, was not in compliance. So the alternative -- and we are facing also the alternative simply of dismissing the request. I am not inclined to give too much time. I will come with a ruling in writing today, or at the latest Monday, to take care of all the points. But I'm not inclined to give a long delay for that. One other question I wanted to raise with the Prosecution. I understand that there are documents being disclosed in these days. I would like to have more information about the disclosure. How far are we with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, a status report on disclosure was filed with the Chamber yesterday. It remains --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: It remains the case, of course, Your Honour, that disclosure is an ongoing obligation for the Prosecution so that notwithstanding any deadlines in the proceedings, there will always continue to be material disclosed. Disclosure -- the processes of disclosure, I perhaps need not detain Your Honour with the mechanics of how that disclosure procedure is conducted, but there is a procedure that is followed. It's been in train. An amount of material was disclosed to the Defence yesterday and disclosure, searches and reviews will continue throughout the course of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Staker. I understand that, that disclosure is a continuing obligation and it has to go on, if new documents are -- have to be disclosed to the Defence. However, it should not be something that could go on for too long. I mean, if -- unless new documents appear. If the documents are in your possession, that should be done quite quickly. I mean, the problem is if you have the documents, I'm not ready to accept that you can disclose them any time during the proceedings. You should do it as soon as possible, as quickly as possible. If new documents arise -- come to you from other sources that you couldn't, of course, control, that's different. But if you are just reviewing what you have to see whether it has to be disclosed, I would like that you do it in a very short time to put the Defence in the position to have these documents and prepare the defence, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: That's understood, Your Honour. In principle the procedure is that periodically a search is done and a review of material that has come into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor since the last review and search was done. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: So in your assessment, how long will it take to review what you have actually?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Well, the aim is to remain up-to-date. We have done disclosure yesterday. And in the future another search and review will be done of material that has come into the Office of the Prosecutor since that search and review. Certain documents have arrived within the Office of the Prosecutor within the last few weeks, so a search and review will be undertaken of that material. And as is evident, new material may come into the Office of the Prosecution, but the aim, in principle as I say, is to periodically conduct reviews of new material that have come in since the last review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Staker. Well, I will urge you to proceed with the disclosure as soon as is feasible. Mr. Kerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERNS
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour. Kurt Kerns. Part of the concern of the Defence is simply that the disclosure of these documents has been as to 17 documents on the eve of the deadline for the filing of our appellate brief. In addition to that, according to paragraph 7 of the Prosecution's status report, apparently it's undisputed that they have material potentially relevant to our appeal, that they're apparently going through it, and have been in possession of it for at least three weeks. That's important because when the Court takes into consideration how much time we've been given to finalise our appeal brief, the Court will take note I was appointed on August 5th to assist with the legal issues. We asked for an extension of our appeal brief deadline which was denied so I'm able to tell the Court we filed our brief this morning. And now, after actually we filed our brief we then come into possession of a document which tells us well, we've got potentially relevant material that we've had for three weeks and we're also giving you 17 pages of documents which I haven't had an opportunity to review. So we're really putting Vinko in a position of saying file your appeal brief before you have all of the relevant information concerning your appeal. So if the Court please, what we would ask for is at least two remedies. One, give us an opportunity to either supplement our Rule 115 argument with any information that might be disclosed from the Prosecution, and two, allow us to supplement our appeal brief, which we have filed, if in fact revelations given to us by the Prosecution call for additional supplementation, because really we're in a position right now of saying to Vinko, file your appeal brief, you can have an extension of your appeal brief but wait, I suppose indefinitely, until the Prosecution gets all their information together and provides it us to under Rule 68. So our remedy that we are requesting, based on the status report that was faxed to us 15 minutes before the close of business yesterday, is to simply say, "Prosecution, you've got a deadline to get us this information by," and "Defence, you have at least I would hope 30 days or so to process that information and supplement either your Rule 115 motion on your appellate brief," because I think to put Vinko in the position of saying your appeal is due before you have all the relevant documents flies in the face of fundamental fairness and due process. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerns. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would echo the sentiments and concerns of Mr. Kerns and Mr. Martinovic, because Mr. Naletilic and his Defence team share those same concerns. Today, as a courtesy copy, the Prosecution handed me this file and this is the 17 documents. I would also tell the Court, Your Honour, that not all of these are even translated into English. Some are only in Serbo-Croatian. The lead counsel does not speak Serbo-Croatian. I do not speak Serbo-Croatian. So we're somewhat hand-tied and hamstrung on some of these documents until they're translated into English. I also share the concern of Mr. Martinovic with the status report stating that -- admitting that they have potentially relevant material to this appeal received in the last three weeks. But what they want to do, Your Honour, is they want to determine whether it's relevant or not. I believe that the proper procedure would be to order the Office of the Prosecutor to give us all those documents and let us determine whether they're relevant for our appeal right now rather than wait another three or four weeks after we -- our deadline is passed to file our brief. I think that would be the only fair way to handle this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand -- sorry. Mr. Staker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: If I might be permitted to respond to the submissions by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: The Prosecution's submission would be that this analysis is somewhat artificial. It's not the case that there is a date by which all material relevant to a case comes into the possession of the Prosecution and then no more material is ever going to materialise so from that date we can disclose and the appeal briefs are filed and the appeal is run. In principle, all relevant material is before the Trial Chamber and formed the basis of the trial judgement. And then on appeal we have deadlines for appeal briefs and argument and so forth. It just remains the case that material will come into the possession of the Prosecution and that will never stop; that will continue throughout the appellate proceedings. And it's not possible to set a cutoff date because that would mean after a certain date there will be no more investigations. The continuing disclosure should not affect the other deadlines in the case. There is a deadline for filing the appeal brief. There may be a deadline for Rule 115 motions and the Prosecution's submission is there should be nothing that requires any change to that. If new material comes into the possession of the Prosecution, it will be disclosed to the Defence. If the Defence, on consideration of that material, feel it's something they want to use in some way - because it may be much of the material we disclose turns out to be of no particular use in the Defence's opinion - but if they want to do something with it then at that point they can file an additional 115 motion and it can be dealt with on its merits. If at that point they feel they've found something that may require a modification or an addition of a new ground of appeal then they can seek leave to do so at that stage. The continuing disclosure by the Prosecution in our submission is an ongoing process. It does not cease and it does not affect the time limits for all the other stages in these appellate proceedings. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Staker. Actually, what I want to say is that -- I agree that the disclosure process is a continuing one. We discussed this earlier. I only urge the Prosecution to proceed as quickly as possible with the disclosure, not to delay the appeal. As to the 115 motion, it is clear that the motion having been filed, if later on documents are disclosed, that the Defence considers should come in as new evidence under Rule 115 and the Defence shows good cause for doing so, a motion can be submitted to admit this new -- to present this new evidence, and I will have no difficulty, as in many other cases, to permit the Defence to file additional 115 motions to take care of these documents. Let's be clear. I will not put in a deadline now, of course, because it really depends on when documents will be disclosed to the Defence. Well, is there any other matter that the parties want to discuss now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have a matter which I believe is relevant to the preparation of this case. Mr. Staker said in principle all evidence was in front of the Trial Chamber. I note that in this new binder which was given us today, there is an indictment or proceeding in the Mostar, in a case number K1:2/95. We have been, for over a year, asking for the Prosecutor to give us all copies of their file in the Mostar case number K5/96. On July of this year we had previously written the Ministry of Defence. We were told by a carbon copy from the Ministry of Defence addressed to the president of the county court of Mostar and the county prosecutor of Mostar asking them what happened to the file - and I refer to it as the lost file. It concerns indictments of individuals in Sovici arising out of the events of 17 of April, 1993, under the Roman rules of the road, the proper procedure would be that the Ministry of Justice would obtain the files from the Office of the Prosecutor and then send them back to the court in Mostar. It is clear -- we believe that the file never reached the Ministry of Defence as it should have. We've sent another letter to the Ministry of Defence on 21 of August. We have not received a reply from that. However, Your Honour, on July 22nd, the Defence for Naletilic sent a letter to the president of the county court of Mostar asking for information regarding this case, the lost file or case number K5/96. We did get an answer to that, which we filed pursuant to Rule 115, and it's been sent for translation. I understand today all those have been translated. That letter stated that the date of the letter, the Mostar court had never received a file from the higher court of the Mostar and the East Mostar court, nor from the higher court of the West Mostar court which was combined into one court about July of 1999. The letter of the county court of Mostar, there's a register which demonstrates that on the 2th of August, 1996, the indictment under KT10/94 and, Your Honour, that's the Prosecutor's number for the same indictment of the court file I referred to earlier, which later became case number K5/96 against certain individuals for war crimes of genocide, war crimes against civilian population, war crimes against war prisoners under the laws of the former Yugoslavia was issued by the Prosecution and received in the court. In the same register, it is written in pencil that a part of the tile was sent to the Ministry of justice, and in brackets "For The Hague" on 22nd of July, 1998. Further, Your Honour, in that register there is no mention of the indictment at all. In the file of K5/96 was not brought to the county court of Mostar after the 19th of July and that was the date the two courts combined in Mostar to make one court. On July 21st, the Defence for Naletilic sent a letter to the county prosecutor for the county of Mostar asking for information. We wanted to know if the case K5/96 was ever returned from the Office of the Prosecutor to the prosecutor in Mostar. We've received no answer. Your Honour, this file is highly important. We believe -- in fact, we know that the Prosecutor has portions of this file because they delivered, finally, towards the end of the Defence case in the middle of the Defence case, two binders. However, those binders did not include the witness statements. The witness statements are what we're after. We cannot find these. We're hitting a brick wall. We don't want the Court to lose sight of the fact that in principle while all relevant evidence should have been before the Trial Chamber, we verily believe that this is highly relevant information. We believe it is sitting in the Office of the Prosecutor somewhere and we believe, with due diligence, they should have found that and given it to us by now. You got to understand, Your Honour, that in this file, the Mostar file K5/96, the one we're looking for, Mr. Naletilic was never indicted, never mentioned in the indictment for any of the crimes that he's been convicted in this court, in this Tribunal of. The judgement, the Trial Chamber judgement inter alia states, paragraph 55, 531 and 532, and also paragraph 32, for example, mention the incidents which occurred in Sovici on or around the 17th of April, 1993. The indictment in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in case number K5/96 is specific as to which persons are responsible for the unlawful transfer of civilians from Sovici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, may I interrupted you? I mean, we are not here to argue the appeal. I mean, you are starting arguing the appeal, and this is not the appropriate place to do it. This is a Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I just want to bring to the Court's attention. My client asked me to bring this to the Court's attention that the Court not lose sight of the fact that we verily believe that the Prosecutor does have this file, these statements. They are highly relevant to this case and we ask that they be turned over. If they can't find them and keep claiming they can't find them, that's fine. I just want Your Honour to know that we're making every effort we can in Mostar, in Herzegovina to find these files and we just keep hit ago brick wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: One moment. [Defence and appellant Naletilic confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, may it please the Court, with all due respect, I don't have a translator here. I do not speak Serbo-Croatian. I would ask to indulge my client. He would like to make a comment to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to address the Prosecution also. I will tell you what this is about. I believe that half of the indictment is based on Sovici and Toljani. I always told my counsel I never set foot in Sovici and evidently, I received only half a sentence for this reason. The court in Mostar has sentenced people to 20, 15, and 10 years in prison for the crimes I have been charged with. We have asked the president of the court for a subpoena to get this court documentation, but our motion was denied. I may be offending the Prosecution and the Tribunal, but I am forced to address the public asking for these documents to come to light. We are asking for witness statements. We have some statements that we have seen, and Tuta was never mentioned in these documents. So, Your Honour, I ask you once again at this higher level to issue a subpoena for these documents. We believe that the Prosecution cares about the truth. And if these documents show that I never so much as set foot in Sovici at the relevant time, that is, the first time I arrived in Sovici was three months after the massacre. So at the relevant time, I never so much as set foot in Sovici. And for the sake of justice, for the sake of the Prosecutor, for the sake of the truth, please let us get hold of these documents so that we can show them to the President of the Tribunal. If Judge Liu refused to issue a subpoena, and we know through various witnesses that my name was never mentioned during that trial and that those documents are here, they're not down there, they're here in the OTP and the OTP received these documents. I believe that you will agree that it would be honest for you to let us have these documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, I take note of what you say, but I have to tell the Defence that any request can be made but must be made according to the Rules of Procedure of this Tribunal. This is the only thing I can say at this stage on this. And the consideration that you make of the substance of the case, that will be taken care of in due course in light of the documents. Well, is there any other matter to be dealt with at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERNS
utterances.text: May it please the Court, just very briefly. I stand the Prosecution's argument that we have a continuing duty to disclose and therefore no deadline should be set. I want to direct the Court's attention to paragraph 7 of the status report which basically says they have right now and have for at least three weeks material potentially relevant to the appeal. So I would ask, certainly at least with regard to that information that they agree they've got right now in their hand, that there shouldn't be a problem with us getting that documentation before I fly out tomorrow, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, may I ask the Prosecution to say how -- may I ask the Prosecution in their assessment now how long it will take to review the material they refer to in paragraph 7 of the status report?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not in a position to say that now. If necessary, perhaps I could give some indication in a filing perhaps within a few days. The information I'm given is that the material we have is not yet electronically searchable and for technical reasons it will take our technical people a certain amount of time to put it in electronically searchable form, and then the disclosure searches are done electronically, and then they have to be viewed by legal staff to determine whether they come within the ambit of Rule 68. So although we're very mindful of our disclosure obligations, these things do simply take a certain amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Staker. Please see to it that it's done as soon as possible and inform the Court and the Defence of the -- of the time that will be needed as soon as you are in the position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, is there any other problem at this stage? I don't think so. In that case, this Status Conference stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
